question: In a colon cancer screening program, a 52-year-old patient undergoes a colonoscopy. The entire colon is normal in appearance, except for the finding of a 2 cm pedicled sigmoid polyp that is removed with a diathermy loop. The anatomopathological result indicates that there is carcinoma "in situ" limited to the head of the polyp. He has a thoracoabdominal CT reported as normal. Indicate what would be the correct conduct to follow:

options.opa: Segmental resection of the affected colon.
options.opc: Local resection of the base of the polyp.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Carcinoma in situ" -> "confined to polyp head" -> "no invasion beyond polyp" -> "normal CT scan" -> "low risk of metastasis" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Carcinoma in situ" -> "confined to polyp head" -> "no invasion beyond polyp" -> "normal CT scan" -> "local resection of polyp base unnecessary" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Carcinoma in situ" -> "confined to polyp head" -> "no invasion beyond polyp" -> "normal CT scan" -> "segmental resection unnecessary" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Carcinoma in situ" -> "confined to polyp head" -> "no invasion beyond polyp" -> "normal CT scan" -> "sigmoidectomy plus lymphadenectomy unnecessary" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance" -> 80%
analysis: The finding of carcinoma 'in situ' in the head of the polyp suggests that the cancerous changes are confined to the epithelial layer and have not invaded deeper tissues. This is considered a non-invasive cancer, and the complete removal of the polyp with clear margins typically suffices as treatment. Given that the CT scan is normal and there is no evidence of invasive cancer, periodic endoscopic surveillance is the appropriate management to monitor for any new polyps or changes.
